subject: history
displayName: KS3 History — Kingship, Magna Carta & Parliament
subtitle: How royal power was challenged and limited from Magna Carta to the rise of Parliament.

data.targetWord: a system of government where a king or queen rules, usually inheriting the crown through a royal family line

examples.en-GB: Medieval monarchy meant the crown usually passed from ruler to ruler within one royal family.

data.targetWord: the belief that a monarch's authority came from God, making kingship seem sacred and difficult to challenge

examples.en-GB: Medieval kings claimed divine right, but they still needed political support from barons and the Church.

data.targetWord: a powerful noble who held land from the king and could provide knights and money, but who could also rebel if the king ruled badly

examples.en-GB: In 1215, rebel barons forced King John to agree to Magna Carta by threatening rebellion.

data.targetWord: being officially excluded from the Christian Church — a serious medieval punishment because religion shaped daily life and ideas about salvation

examples.en-GB: King John was excommunicated in 1209, damaging his legitimacy as a Christian ruler.

data.targetWord: a Church punishment that stopped many religious services across a whole kingdom, creating fear because people worried about being cut off from the sacraments

examples.en-GB: England was placed under interdict in 1208 during Pope Innocent III's dispute with King John.

data.targetWord: the 'Great Charter' agreed in 1215 at Runnymede between King John and rebel barons, which tried to limit some royal abuses and protect certain rights of free men, nobles, and the Church

examples.en-GB: Magna Carta was agreed in June 1215 and later became a symbol of the rule of law.

data.targetWord: a written document granting rights, privileges, or promises — Magna Carta means 'Great Charter' in Latin

examples.en-GB: The charter was written in Latin and contained many clauses about taxation, justice, and Church freedoms.

data.targetWord: money paid instead of providing knights for military service — King John demanded it heavily, which angered many barons

examples.en-GB: Scutage was one of the main financial complaints of barons against King John before 1215.

data.targetWord: agreement or permission — in medieval politics, this usually meant powerful groups such as barons agreeing to taxation before the king could collect it

examples.en-GB: Magna Carta suggested that certain payments should not be imposed without the consent of important political groups.

data.targetWord: a political assembly that developed from royal councils, where kings sought advice and taxation; it became important for law and representation but was not democratic in the modern sense

examples.en-GB: Medieval Parliament was not the same as modern Parliament — most people could not vote or be directly represented.

data.targetWord: the idea that some people speak or act on behalf of others — in medieval Parliament, knights and burgesses represented shires and towns

examples.en-GB: De Montfort's Parliament of 1265 was significant because it included knights and burgesses as representatives.

data.targetWord: the belief that a ruler has the right to rule — a medieval king needed both military power and legitimacy to govern effectively

examples.en-GB: John's excommunication damaged his legitimacy because a Christian king was expected to cooperate with the Church.

data.targetWord: the Parliament called by Edward I in 1295, which included archbishops, bishops, abbots, earls, barons, knights from each shire, and burgesses from boroughs — it became an important example for later Parliaments

examples.en-GB: Edward I called the Model Parliament in 1295 partly to gain broader consent for taxation to fund his wars.

data.targetWord: reforms forced on Henry III in 1258 by barons who wanted to limit royal government and increase consultation with a baronial council

examples.en-GB: The Provisions of Oxford show that even after Magna Carta, tensions over royal power continued under Henry III.

data.targetWord: a powerful noble who led opposition to Henry III and called a Parliament in 1265 that included knights and burgesses, making it significant in the history of representation

examples.en-GB: Simon de Montfort's 1265 Parliament was significant because it included wider representation than earlier royal councils.

data.targetWord: the meadow near the River Thames where King John agreed to Magna Carta in June 1215

examples.en-GB: Today, Runnymede is remembered as the place where King John sealed Magna Carta.

data.targetWord: armed resistance against a ruler or government — in 1215, barons organised rebellion against King John to force him to agree to Magna Carta

examples.en-GB: Baronial rebellion was a key cause of Magna Carta because the barons had to put military pressure on John.

data.targetWord: a battle in 1214 where John's allies were defeated by King Philip II of France, damaging John's prestige and encouraging baronial rebellion in England

examples.en-GB: After the Battle of Bouvines in 1214, barons believed John had failed despite taking large amounts of their money.

data.targetWord: the collection of money by a ruler or government — medieval kings needed taxation for war, castles, officials, and royal government

examples.en-GB: The link between taxation and consent was central to the development of Parliament.

data.targetWord: the principle that even rulers must obey the law — Magna Carta contributed to this idea, especially in later centuries when it became a symbol of legal limits on royal power

examples.en-GB: Magna Carta's later significance was tied to the rule of law — the idea that no one, not even a king, is above the law.

data.targetWord: King of England from 1199 to 1216, whose military failures in France, conflicts with the Pope, and heavy taxation led directly to baronial rebellion and Magna Carta in 1215

examples.en-GB: King John lost Normandy in 1204 and was excommunicated in 1209 before facing baronial rebellion in 1215.

data.targetWord: a representative from a town or borough who attended Parliament — burgesses were included in de Montfort's 1265 Parliament and Edward I's 1295 Model Parliament

examples.en-GB: Including burgesses in Parliament meant that towns had some representation alongside nobles and Church leaders.

data.targetWord: one of the most powerful medieval popes, who clashed with King John over the Archbishop of Canterbury, then later supported John against the rebel barons and annulled Magna Carta

examples.en-GB: Pope Innocent III annulled Magna Carta shortly after it was agreed, showing that John was not committed to keeping it.

data.targetWord: a region in northern France that was connected to English kings since 1066 — King John lost it to Philip II of France in 1204, damaging his prestige and triggering heavier taxation

examples.en-GB: The loss of Normandy in 1204 was a major cause of baronial anger because barons paid for campaigns that failed.

data.targetWord: the civil war of 1215-1217 that followed Magna Carta, showing that the charter failed to bring immediate peace — some rebels invited Prince Louis of France to take the English throne

examples.en-GB: The First Barons' War shows that Magna Carta was not an immediate success in ending conflict between John and the barons.

data.targetWord: King of England from 1216 to 1272, who became king as a child, saw Magna Carta reissued in 1225, and faced baronial opposition led by Simon de Montfort over how he governed

examples.en-GB: Henry III's favouritism towards foreign advisers and expensive foreign policy led barons to force the Provisions of Oxford in 1258.

data.title: Key events leading to Magna Carta in chronological order
items: King John loses Normandy to France (1204)
England placed under interdict by Pope Innocent III (1208)
John makes peace with the Pope (1213)
John's allies defeated at the Battle of Bouvines (1214)
Rebel barons force John to agree Magna Carta at Runnymede (1215)

data.title: Development of Parliament in chronological order
items: Magna Carta links taxation to common counsel (1215)
Barons force Henry III to accept Provisions of Oxford (1258)
Simon de Montfort's Parliament includes knights and burgesses (1265)
Edward I calls the Model Parliament (1295)

data.title: The cause-consequence chain of baronial rebellion and Magna Carta
items: John raises heavy scutage to fund campaigns to recover Normandy
Defeat at Bouvines (1214) convinces barons John has failed
John agrees to Magna Carta at Runnymede (June 1215)
John asks the Pope to annul the charter
